title.title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability
title.subtitle: Claim: von Neumann algebras close enough are conjugate by a unitary near 1, with a universal tolerance

beats.text: Schematic: two von Neumann algebras on one Hilbert space, unit balls within $\delta$
Claim: a unitary $u$ with $\lVert u - 1 \rVert < \varepsilon$ carries one exactly onto the other
and $\delta$ depends only on $\varepsilon$: not on the algebras or the space

achievement.label: Kadison–Kastler conjecture (1972), strong form
achievement.context: Before: injective algebras, separable nuclear C*-algebras (2012), some II$_1$ factors (2014)

verify.detail: Universal strong stability for von Neumann algebras; the counterexamples are paper-only
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

plain: If two algebras of operators are almost the same, a tiny rotation turns one exactly into the other

steps: Pair each unitary of one algebra with a nearby one in the other
Correct the pairs by averaging so they multiply consistently
A uniform commutator bound turns this into one small rotation

voice.text: Two von Neumann algebras on one space, with unit balls within delta.
Match nearby unitaries, average to fix their products, and control every matrix level.
Claimed: a tiny rotation matches them exactly.
